note: Government housing laws/programs relevant to sub-$600k investors. Demand-side federal schemes concentrate buyer competition at affordable price points; state planning reforms create land-value uplift near transport.

federal.name: Help to Buy (shared equity)
federal.detail: Government takes up to 40% equity (new) / 30% (existing); buyer needs 2% deposit. No cap on places and no income limits since 1 Oct 2025.
federal.investor_read: Adds a large pool of assisted owner-occupier buyers competing for affordable stock (<$600k) — supports capital growth of entry-level houses/townhouses.

federal.name: First Home Guarantee (5% deposit, no LMI)
federal.detail: No income caps, no annual place limit, 5% deposit (2% single parents). Sydney price cap raised to $1.5M.
federal.investor_read: Uncapped first-home demand at affordable price points nationwide — a structural bid under sub-$600k markets.

federal.name: $10B housing supply fund (May 2026 Budget)
federal.detail: Targets 100,000 homes built and sold to first home buyers below market price.
federal.investor_read: Adds new supply at the affordable end over time — modest headwind to scarcity in greenfield areas; watch supply-heavy corridors.

federal.name: Housing Australia Future Fund
federal.investor_read: Mostly social housing — limited direct effect on owner-occupier/investor price points.

state.name: Low & Mid-Rise Housing + Transport Oriented Development (TOD)
state.status: In force from 2025; EP&A Act reforms Dec 2025
state.detail: R3 zones near TOD precincts allow residential flat buildings up to FSR 2.2:1 / 6 storeys; state-led rezonings + pattern book to speed approvals.
state.investor_read: Land-value uplift for houses on larger blocks within ~400–800m of nominated stations/centres — a targeted capital-growth catalyst.

state.name: Activity Centres Plan + Mid-Rise Code
state.status: Mid-Rise Code operational 16 Apr 2026; 60 stations rezoned
state.detail: Land rezoned around ~60 train/tram locations (apartments up to 20 storeys in centres); 10 pilot activity centres finalised 2025, +50 more staged.
state.investor_read: Sites within activity-centre catchments gain redevelopment potential — favour houses on subdividable land near nominated centres.

state.name: First-home stamp-duty exemption (new builds)
state.status: From 1 May 2025; off-the-plan concession to 21 Oct 2026
state.detail: First home buyers exempt from transfer duty on newly built homes / vacant land; investors still pay standard duty.
state.investor_read: Tilts first-home demand toward NEW townhouses/house-and-land — supports new-build values in SEQ growth corridors.

state.name: Density & planning reform (top scorecard 2026)
state.detail: SA & WA rank highest in the 2026 HIA planning reform scorecard; Adelaide density reform push.
state.investor_read: Faster approvals + gentle density support supply response but also uplift near corridors — constructive for Adelaide/Perth mid-ring.
